unmapped_findings: IA750_60 Min specimen exhibits the highest product of ultimate tensile strength and total elongation (PSE = 7.9 GPa%) among HRQ and all annealing conditions, attributed to enhanced TRIP effect from optimum mechanical stability of the reverted austenite [b0046, b0066, table_003].
Mechanical stability parameter K of the IA750_60 Min specimen is ~1.92, supporting optimum (intermediate) mechanical stability of its needle+globular reverted austenite [b0061, figure_007].
The IA750_60 Min specimen shows the highest transformation ratio of austenite (~20%) during tensile loading, consistent with the highest PSE via enhanced TRIP effect [b0061, figure_007].

Theoretical SFE of the reverted austenite in IA750_60 Min (Mn 7.58±0.14, Al 3.96±0.15 wt.%, C ~0.05 wt.%) is calculated as ~27 mJ/m², lower than the equilibrium-composition SFE of ~35 mJ/m², explaining TRIP as the dominant deformation mechanism [b0073].
The work hardening rate (mean WHR) of IA750_60 Min in stage S2 is the highest among annealed specimens, between 2000-1000 MPa, leading to the maximum UTS and TE [b0051, figure_006].
No TWIP effect was observed in these high SFE alloys, and the plastic region of the stress-strain curve showed no serrations [b0073].

Fracture surface of the IA750_60 Min tensile specimen shows quasi-cleavage with dimpled ductile-tearing regions; the intercritical ferrite contributes cleavage whereas reverted austenite contributes dimples [b0072, figure_011].
No carbide (such as κ-carbide) or elemental clustering was detected in the IA750_60 Min specimen by SEM, HRTEM/EDS or APT analyses [b0066, b0067, b0071].
The globular-shaped reverted austenite in IA750_60 Min has an average diameter of 0.0185±0.010 µm and is lean in Mn and C due to elemental partitioning to adjacent untransformed austenite [b0064].
δ-ferrite in the IA750_60 Min specimen remains highly stable (composition nearly constant across annealing times), attributed to the high Al and Si content [b0039, b0042, figure_004].
